cards.text: A plague has just ended in Israel. Then the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest. And friend, He's got a job for them that's gonna need a LOT of fingers. I use my mustache as hands and even I'd run out.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Moses and Eleazar to do?

cards.text: Big job. But the LORD isn't asking for every single person on this list.

cards.question: Who does the LORD want counted in this census?

answers.text: Men twenty and up who can serve in the army
Only the leaders of each family line
Every firstborn son from every tribe

cards.text: So Moses and Eleazar pass the order along: count the men, just like the LORD commanded. Hope somebody brought a pencil. A BIG one.

cards.question: Where is Israel when Moses and Eleazar give the order to count?

answers.text: The plains of Moab across from Jericho
Kadesh in the Desert of Zin
The shore of the Red Sea

cards.text: Then the count goes tribe by tribe, clan by clan, with a total for each one. The list pauses for a few names, like Dathan and Abiram, who rebelled with Korah's followers and were swallowed by the earth, though Korah's line didn't die out. And Zelophehad, who had no sons, only five daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah. Final total: 601,730 men. Back in the junk drawer I used to count the dust falling, and I never once made it past forty.
Count's done. Then the LORD tells Moses what all those names are for: the land is to be divided among the tribes as an inheritance, according to the number of names. See? The counting PAYS OFF.

cards.question: Under the LORD's plan, a large tribe gets a bigger inheritance than a small tribe.
The LORD says each tribe's inheritance of land must be divided by ___.

cards.text: The Levites get counted on their own: 23,000 males a month old or more. They aren't numbered with the other Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites. Their list even names Amram and Jochebed, the parents of Aaron, Moses and their sister Miriam.
Now here's the twist, friend. There was an earlier count, taken by Moses and Aaron the priest in the Wilderness of Sinai. So you'd figure a few familiar names show up on this new list. Right? …Right?

cards.question: Some of the men counted at Sinai show up again in this new count on the plains of Moab.
The LORD had told the men of that first count that they would surely ___ in the wilderness.
Not one man from the Sinai count is left except two. Who are they?

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: the plague, the LORD speaking to Moses and Eleazar, the 'fingers' line, and the mustache line.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The joke 'I use my mustache as hands and even I'd run out' doesn't hold up. The setup is about counting on fingers, but a mustache has no fingers to run out of. The image blurs, and a stranger would say 'huh?' It also uses the mustache as the main source of the joke.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action. ... It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The summary card for the census list is five sentences long. It gives two separate standout details, Dathan and Abiram with Korah, and then Zelophehad with all five daughters' names. It also adds the total and a joke. That is far more than a few words and close to going item by item.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. He can name a standout detail the text gives if it helps the stretch stick.

findings.problem: Korah shows up for the first time ('Korah's followers', 'Korah's line') without a word on who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The setup gives away card 13's answer. 'Now here's the twist' and the doubtful 'Right? …Right?' tell the baker the expected answer is False before they pick.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The statement 'Some of the men counted at Sinai show up again in this new count' is marked False. But Numbers 26:65 says 'Not one was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.' Card 15 itself says two men from the Sinai count are left. So the 'wrong' answer, True, is arguably right elsewhere in the passage, and a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Caleb and Joshua appear for the first time as the answer, with nothing saying who they are, for example Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun, the two who survived from the first count.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
